### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**38** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3d2d460b2a807d73f191b1daa6619f016a1c8814` — the merge of head `733b0e6815e750e41fdcb3b23efa15cbb799323c` into base `4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3d2d460b2a807d73f191b1daa6619f016a1c8814 && git checkout 3d2d460b2a807d73f191b1daa6619f016a1c8814
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb 733b0e6815e750e41fdcb3b23efa15cbb799323c && git checkout -B drift-repro 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb && git merge --no-ff 733b0e6815e750e41fdcb3b23efa15cbb799323c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4b4ee88fbc530a155ce3ea0570ad81d905d3afbb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `733b0e6815e750e41fdcb3b23efa15cbb799323c`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, at tier, adversarial to the dispatch. Inputs: card #20513 (body and all 13 comments — the census 5900801368, the ruling 5902360492 「20513 A」 A / A, the lane checklist 5902678544, the services pointer 5903999785, the stage-1 claim 5904785587, the stage-1 `os-dev-report` 5905390342), PR #20795 (body, 12-file list, the net diff `origin/main...733b0e6815` at merge base `085ca6bc1`), PR #20738 at `5a23096ca` as the form-D precedent, the head's check-runs, the cited cards, and the head's own source through `git show`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on `733b0e6815` (read for this record, 2026-09-30T07:15Z):** 34 check-runs, all `completed`: 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — path-filtered). The seven required contexts all conclude `success`: Lint & Repo Gates (carries `check:doc-authoring`), TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also `success`: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Part-of PR must not also close its card, the claim and single-writer guards. Nothing `in_progress`.

### ① Derived judgments

**Scope against the ruling and the claim — right.** The ruling orders stages per package until the ledger is empty, all three categories, form D, `--census-ledger` in the same PR; the claim scopes stage 1 to `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/**`, the pins, the ledger and one `patch` changeset, and forbids wire `code` / field / status changes, comment edits and other packages' ledger rows. The 12-file list is exactly that surface: 4 source files, 6 test files, the ledger, the changeset. No governed path.

**Text only — right, checked line by line.** Every removed and added line in `sql-driver.ts` (117 lines), `schema-drift.ts` (10), `cross-field-conformance-cases.ts` (12) and `live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts` (2) is inside a string literal (a template or quoted `+` chain, or a `note:` value). No `err.code`, `err.status`, `StandardErrorCode` member, exported symbol, field name, branch or call moves; the `d.message = nullSafeKey ? … : …` ternary and every `logger.*` / `logDurabilityFailure` call keep their shape. Comments and docblocks are untouched, as the claim requires. The six test-file changes are the 18 pin lines only.

**Accept-set and public surface — nothing moves — right.** No schema, filter grammar, DDL, route or export changes; a caller sees different prose in the same envelopes with the same `code` and `status`. driver-turso's byte-parity tests are the only cross-package readers of these strings, and Test Core is green on them.

**Ledger diff — right, exact.** Only four `driver-sql` entries move: `cross-field-conformance-cases.ts` (6 occurrences, 5 pairs), `schema-drift.ts` (4 / 4) and `live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts` (1 / 1) leave; `sql-driver.ts` goes from 32 pairs / 62 occurrences to 3 / 3 (`#10413`, `#5907`, `#6409`, one each). 73 to 3. I reconciled the removed occurrences against the source diff id by id: 59 removed from `sql-driver.ts` (`#7929` ×7, `#11627` ×7, `#8197` ×5, `#5030` ×5, `#13015` ×3, `#13056` ×3, `#5907` 2 to 1, and the rest one or two each) plus 6 + 4 + 1 in the other three files — every removed occurrence is a citation deleted in the diff, and no other package's row moves. A `git grep` of the head over the four files finds exactly three non-comment tracker-id hits, the held ones at `sql-driver.ts` 1674, 1778 and 1812. `check:doc-authoring` inside the green Lint & Repo Gates run is the mechanical confirmation (the dev's local read: 732 pinned sites across 224 files, no burn-down unrecorded).

**Form D, string by string — right.** I judged each sentence against its cited card — or, for the five that answer 404 (11067, 11374, 12380, 12999, 13015), against the landing commit and today's docblock: `479fba50df`, route A of #11374 `3954fb7df5`, `4045b954d3`, `ebcc34e893`, `cd1348802e` / `431d2fb42a` — and against the head's code. All 35 readable objectstack cards are closed and completed; no cited decision has been reversed. Where words were added:
- `reference_to` DDL refusal (3896, 11567): "raw `registerObject` skips Zod" and "the FK DDL this key used to gate is retired, because it could never fire for a spec-conformant lookup" — the function's own docblock (about 1900-1915) states both, with the zero-FK measurement; #11567 is the finding that led to the retirement. True.
- NULL-safe UNIQUE (5030, five sites): "SQL UNIQUE is NULL-distinct, so it never constrained rows without an organization" — #5030's title and its step 4 say exactly this. True at 13532, 14020, 14778, 14860 and 14951.
- Foreign column in the hash-shadow slot (11627, 13015): "it may hold data" — the inline comment beside the `state === 'foreign'` branch (about 18308) says the same. True.
- SQLite canonicalisation info lines (3912, 3994, 12380): the datetime and time lines name the one text form and why it matters (filters and sorts compare like with like), the json line names JSON-encoded strings as the one encoding a json column holds on every dialect — matching the three backfill docblocks, #3912 / #3994's root causes, and `4045b954d3` ("one encoding across all three dialects"). True.
- MySQL widening (3942, 3994): "TIMESTAMP ends at 2038-01-19, keeps no milliseconds and converts through the session timezone" is #3942 §1 / §2 and the `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns` docblock; "a zero-precision TIME rounds the canonical milliseconds to the nearest second" is the `migrateMysqlTimeColumns` docblock and #3994 F4. True.
- Case notes (5146, 7597, cloud 1051, 7398, 5041): `$not` NULL-safe by totalised leaves is what #5146 asked for and what the old note recorded as done; the `=`-spelling lowering to `$eq` is live in the same file (`EQUALITY_SPELLINGS`, `loweredTo: { $eq: { $field } }`, about 293-331); "only a declared column reaches SQL" is corroborated by #5041's body (放行不校验等于拆护栏), since cloud#1051 is not readable from this repository; the JSON-column note and the "compiled `$field` comparands, refused the rest" note match #7398 and #5041's enforce outcome. True.
Where only the citation goes (5158, 5240, 5347 / 5369, 5348, 6050, 6212, 7929 / 8197 / 8220, 8790, 8931, 11067, 11374, 11541, 11565, 12999, 13056, 4363, 4560, 3696, 11535, 12121, 9350, and 5907 at 1749): the sentence already carried the decision and is unchanged; each card's title matches its sentence; the 6212 sentence's mechanism (`supports.queryDateGranularity`, engine buckets in memory) is live at `objectql/src/engine.ts` about 16581-16587.

**Pins — right, 18 lines in 6 files.** Each number pin moved to the phrase that carries the decision: `NULL-distinct` ×12 (7 of them negative pins, whose meaning holds because the plain-unique branches at about 13541-13549 and 14790-14840 never say it), the declare-`maxLength` sentence and the absence of "re-declaring `maxLength` changes nothing here" ×5, "receives one opaque id instead of a list" ×1. Each asserted phrase is present in the head's string. The MySQL-only 15479 file's three pins are exercised by Temporal Conformance, which runs the whole `driver-sql` suite against live PG and MySQL (`ci.yml` about 1266 onward) — green.

**Two wording notes, not FAIL items (carrier: a later stage of this lane, or whoever next edits these lines):** (a) the datetime and time "every value is now one … text form" info line can print beside the warn that follows it naming withheld bare-numeric rows; "every converted value" would be exact. (b) at about 14020 the failed-restore arm reads "Rows without an organization are not constrained, because SQL UNIQUE is NULL-distinct", while the reason in that arm is that no index exists at all; the statement is not false and the remedy it gives is right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20513-driver-sql-runtime-strings-state-the-decision.md`: `@objectstack/driver-sql: patch` — right. The diff publishes changed prose in one released package and nothing else; no key, export, envelope `code`, status or default moves, so this is a fix-class patch, never `skip-changeset`. The changeset body is CHANGELOG-fit: it names the message families that changed, states "text only", and says why three aggregate refusals keep their citation for now. No model identifier in the changeset, the commit trailers or the PR body (session-URL footer on the body; the commit carries the model-free trailer pair).

Clause-②: no — right. Nothing an author can write is widened or narrowed; the PR body carries `Clause-②: no` at line start and the changeset repeats it. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (report 5905390342), each answered:
1. **Three aggregate refusals held (`#5907` at 1674, `#10413` at 1778, `#6409` at 1812), handed to the driver-turso stage — accepted.** `remote-transport-aggregate-function-refusal.test.ts` about 348 and 510 assert `remote.message` equal to `local.message` for the undeclared-function class, about 576 asserts the per-aggregation-`filter` refusal equal after a backend-name substitution, and `remote-transport-undeclared-aggregate-keys.test.ts` about 201 asserts the same byte equality; the field-less `count_distinct` refusal is compared by the block at about 394. The twins in `remote-transport.ts` carry the same citations, and the claim forbids touching another package's ledger rows, so one face cannot move alone. The stage-4 carrier is named in the dev's out_of_scope_findings and the PR's acceptance notes; that stage's ledger diff will move these three `driver-sql` rows as well. Held, not lost.
2. **Two twins now differ by the citation only (5907 uncompiled at 1749 / remote about 987; 6212 date bucket at 1867 / remote about 1108) — accepted.** The remote copies still end in `(#5907)` / `(#6212)`; the pinned contract is first-sentence parity (`remote-transport-groupby-node.test.ts` about 462-463; the aggregate test's class-2 comparison is gone since `count_distinct` compiles on both faces), and it holds. The remote numbers go with the driver-turso stage.
3. **62 literals in one PR, under the ~80 stop line — accepted.** The ruling's "author-visible text first, log lines last" orders stages that must be split; a stage that lands whole has nothing left to order.
4. **Withheld-detail sentences left at deletion only — accepted, and correct.** `remote-transport-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts` about 489-494 asserts the remote withheld message equals `'[RemoteTransport] '` plus the local one, and `remote-transport.ts` already reads "withheld from the message; the full diagnostic is in the server log" (about 837, 3686, 3718, 3751, 3903). Adding words on the local face would have broken that pin; the deletion makes the two faces identical.
5. **18 re-pins — verified in ①.**
6. **Live PG / MySQL NOT MEASURED locally — CI's, and green** (Temporal Conformance `success`).

`open_questions`: none in the stage-1 report; none raised here. The PR body's numbers reconcile: 41 distinct cited ids = 35 closed objectstack cards + 5 that answer 404 + cloud#1051; census 52 messages against ledger 73 occurrences reconciles through the `+`-chain folding and the 7 `src`-shipped test strings, as the body states. The card's lane children (#20749, #20751, #20753, `Blocked-by: #20513`) are unaffected by this stage.
